key_insight: Pixel MeanFlow (pMF) enables one-step, latent-free image generation by separating the network output space from the loss space and learning a pixel-wise mean flow mapping directly in image space, removing the need for multi-step sampling or a latent bottleneck.
problem_solved: Modern diffusion and flow models rely on multi-step sampling and operate in latent spaces, which increases sampling time and complicates model design; pMF addresses fast, high-quality image generation without latents or iterative denoising.
method: Design a network that predicts a pixel-wise mean flow mapping directly in image (pixel) space rather than a latent representation.
Separate the network output space from the loss space so the model can optimize a loss that differs from the raw output representation (e.g., transform-domain or perceptual loss) to improve fidelity.
Train the mapping to produce a one-step deterministic or single-sample stochastic transform from noise to image, enabling one-step sampling at inference.
impact: pMF simplifies generation pipelines and dramatically reduces sampling cost while retaining high-quality outputs, making fast, end-to-end image synthesis more practical for real-world ML workflows and deployment.

paper_title: One-step Latent-free Image Generation with Pixel Mean Flows
paper_authors: Yiyang Lu, Susie Lu, Qiao Sun, Hanhong Zhao, Zhicheng Jiang
